title: Maintenance for live-in partners - the legal position today
p1:
Can a person in a live-in relationship claim maintenance after separation? The answer is not as simple as many people think.

A common belief is that only a legally married spouse can seek financial support. But the law has evolved, and certain live-in relationships may receive legal protection.
p2:
Courts have recognised that every live-in relationship does not automatically create a right to maintenance. The relationship must have the characteristics of a marriage-like partnership, such as stability, shared life, and mutual responsibilities.

The surprising part: simply living together for some time may not be enough. The nature of the relationship matters more than just the duration.
p3:
The practical takeaway is that people in live-in relationships should understand their rights and responsibilities before financial disputes arise. Courts look at facts and circumstances, not just labels.

Legal protection depends on the specific situation, so assumptions can lead to costly mistakes.
conclusion: Do you think long-term live-in partners should have the same maintenance rights as married couples? Share your view.
